title: Chapter 8: The Azure Arrow Talisman
paragraphs: The Immortal Sect had inherited many systems from Diyuan Star's previous civilization. For instance, any Medicinal Pill placed on the market was required to have its complete ingredient list prominently displayed on the packaging.
In other words, every Medicinal Pill sold came with its complete formula.
However, attempting to refine a finished product based solely on the formula listed on the pill's label was virtually impossible.

The fusion of modern pharmaceutical technology with traditional alchemy was so intricate that it could take days to explain all the nuances. Thus, while pill formulas were public knowledge, the refinement and production of Medicinal Pills remained a monopolized industry.

Moreover, each university and Dao Academy invested vast resources into researching new Medicinal Pills. It was only fair that they profited from their efforts; without the Immortal Sect's subsidies, no one would be willing to invest in the pharmaceutical industry.
The Purple Fire Pill from Chi Xia Academy was specifically designed to aid practitioners in breaking through to the Mid-Stage Qi Refinement realm.

For those advancing from the Fourth Layer of Qi Refinement to the Fifth, the Purple Fire Pill boasted a success rate of approximately 60-70%. However, for those attempting to break through from the Fifth Layer to the Sixth, the success rate plummeted by more than half, dropping to a mere 20-30%.

Furthermore, if cultivators with a strong Water Spiritual Root took the pill, its efficacy would be halved. Conversely, those with dominant Wood and Fire Spiritual Roots could increase their success rate by another ten percent.
Even with these caveats, the Purple Fire Pill remained the most popular medicinal pill within its tier.
Its gentle medicinal properties and Chi Xia Academy's centuries of refinement had achieved a state of near-perfect purity, eliminating all traces of pill toxicity.
After consumption, just ten to fifteen days of nurturing with the Immortal Sect's common Qi Nourishment Technique would resolve any side effects from the forced breakthrough.
Chen Mobai's luck proved exceptional.

The Purple Fire Pill's primary ingredient was the Purple Sun Sunflower, unique to Danxia City, containing a trace of Yang Fire Purple Qi. Nourishing it with Water Spiritual Energy would yield double the benefits with half the effort.
The Water Abode happened to be constructed atop a Second-Tier Mid-Grade Water Spiritual Vein, where Water Spiritual Energy was exceptionally dense.
Two days later, Chen Mobai opened his eyes with a look of delighted surprise.
Feeling his Spiritual Power flowing freely within him, as if it were an extension of his own limbs, he confirmed that his Fifth Layer of Qi Refinement realm had completely stabilized.
This took even less time than he had anticipated, a testament to his underestimation of the potency of a Second-Tier Mid-Grade Water Spiritual Vein's Spiritual Energy.
However, this couldn't be blamed on him. As a child from an ordinary family, he had never cultivated in a Spiritual Land of this caliber before.
He retrieved the box of glass beads he had purchased earlier.
One, two, three... By the fifth bead, a radiant glow began to emanate, and it slowly lifted from Chen Mobai's palm. A joyful smile spread across his face.
I might actually reach the Sixth Layer of Qi Refinement before the college entrance exams,he thought.
He stood up and stretched languidly.
Chen Mobai began to examine the Water Abode once more.
Everything remained unchanged, just as it always had been.

Over the past two days, he had consulted Old Man Ding again, feigning that his private tutor, impressed by his rapid progress, had increased the difficulty of his assignments, presenting him with the formidable challenge of the Compound Restriction.

Old Man Ding, believing his own guidance had been remarkably effective, felt immensely gratified. After meticulously inquiring about the Compound Restriction's characteristics, he drew upon his extensive teaching experience to propose two distinct methods for breaking it.
The first method, similar to Chen Mobai's initial idea, involved using powerful Restriction-Breaking Talismans to bombard the Restriction's weakest point, breaking it through brute force.

The second approach advocated for finesse over force. While the Compound Restriction was formidable, its complexity stemmed from its intricate combination of interconnected spells, each relying on the others. By disrupting even a single spell, the entire structure would destabilize, causing the remaining spells to falter and become inoperative.
If the person who cast the Restriction lacked expertise, the disruption of a single spell could even trigger the remaining spells to clash, leading to the entire structure collapsing spontaneously.
Old Man Ding, a proud man himself, offered Chen Mobai a second solution.

This method required using a magical artifact imbued with Wood Attribute Spiritual Power to sever the Water Abode Spiritual Vein's Spiritual Energy supply. Once the Compound Restriction revealed itself, Chen Mobai could then dismantle each layer using corresponding techniques.

However, Chen Mobai was practically penniless. His only magical artifact was a child's version of the Demon-Subduing Sword hanging in his room. Enhanced with a Light Spell, it barely qualified as a First-Tier Low-Grade ornamental artifact.
After checking the Immortal Sect Online Marketplace, he discovered that the cheapest Wood Attribute artifact meeting the requirements cost at least 500 Merit Points.
Forced to revert to the first method, Chen Mobai reluctantly retrieved three talismans etched with azure arrows from his pocket, his face twisted in pain.
These were First-Tier Mid-Grade Azure Arrow Talismans, each worth 35 Merit Points.
After two days of tutelage from Old Man Ding, Chen Mobai had learned that the best approach for dismantling unfamiliar Water Attribute Restrictions was to use Wood Attribute Spells or talismans.
According to the Five Elements, attacking Water with Fire would naturally be most effective.

However, if the Water Attribute Restriction's hidden power far exceeded pre-assessment estimates, the violent reaction between Water and Fire Spiritual Power could engulf the Restriction-Breaker, potentially leading to their immediate demise.
Wood counters Water, and its stimulation of Water Attribute Spiritual Power is less violent than Fire's. Even if the Restriction's power is unusually strong, the aftershocks will be relatively mild.
The power of the Azure Arrow Talisman is comparable to the Water Sword Talisman that Chen Mobai had previously considered and added to his shopping cart.

When activated, the Water Sword Talisman conjures a transparent, flowing longsword of water, its form shifting at will and its movements as fluid as thought, capable of lasting for up to fifteen minutes.
In contrast, the Azure Arrow Talisman materializes azure long arrows based on the user's cultivation level, capable of firing up to six in a single burst.
As a Fifth-Stage Qi Refinement cultivator, Chen Mobai can unleash five arrows with a single activation.
Though somewhat wasteful, this talisman remains the most suitable for breaking the Restriction.

To ensure a successful breakthrough in one fell swoop, Chen Mobai exhausted his savings and even sold all the blank talisman paper he had painstakingly cut and accumulated during his spare time, barely scraping together the Merit Points needed to purchase these three Azure Arrow Talismans.

"If there's nothing valuable inside after breaking the Restriction, I'll be spitting blood from the loss," Chen Mobai muttered to himself, gathering his spiritual power. He even activated his Wood Armor Talisman, imbuing it with spiritual power in advance, ready to defend against any unexpected aftershocks from the impending breakthrough.
Just then, the sound of rushing water echoed through the air.
Chen Mobai stared in disbelief as a hole opened in the spherical barrier enveloping the entire Water Abode, and two figures descended.
The pair consisted of an old man and a young man.
The elder's hair was streaked with gray, and he carried a black flag, yet his eyes shone with sharp intensity.
The younger man had an ordinary face and wore a brown robe. Upon landing, he immediately maintained a two-meter distance from the elder.
The two newcomers and Chen Mobai, who stood in the Front Hall, formed a perfect triangle, each sizing up the others warily.
